answer: Like a tide that only lets strong swimmers reach the vault, an agent economy can demand a small proof-of-work puzzle for every new identity before it may earn. Each puzzle costs real compute, so a Sybil farmer who wants a thousand fake agents must pay for a thousand puzzles — the cost echoes across every copy. Honest agents solve once and keep working; the attacker pays again for each fake, and the bill grows faster than any profit from the attack.
